that since earlier it dealt with halachah,
it brings this to conclude on a good note.
But why did they choose this aggadah?
that so we find with the early prophets,
there it is his own words of prophecy,
and he took care to conclude on a good note;
and presumably there is a connection
in each prophet in the pasuk with which he concludes,
so that it fits the theme of that prophet's prophecy.
where it is an earlier statement
is brought in the Gemara, Megillah (28b),
as is implied by the Gemara there just before,
in the matter of one who studies halachos,
and likewise, "who used to study halachah," etc.,
וְעַל זֶה קָאֵי הָא דְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ
and to this refers the teaching of Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu,
But here, where just before they were discussing
and those are not arranged for study at all,
what connection is there after it
and his intent also seems to be
And perhaps one may explain their intent
according to what they said in the Yerushalmi
are all embedded in the Mishnah," etc.;
and that is why he calls the mishnayos
that he is a ben Olam Haba" —
have a share in Olam Haba;
"that he is a ben Olam Haba."
that he is assured he will not go astray
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בִּכְלַל הַמְּנוּיִין
and will not, chas v'shalom, be among those listed
בַּמִּשְׁנָה בְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
in the Mishnah as having no share in Olam Haba.
For if he goes astray and becomes one of them,
his studying halachos will not help;
and if so, it should have said,
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
"He is assured that he will be a ben Olam Haba,"
and not in the present tense,
"that he is a ben Olam Haba."
וְכֵן דִּקְדַּקְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ד, ב):
And likewise we noted what they said (Berachos 4b),
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא —
is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba" —
this too is difficult, as mentioned above.
And just before it (ibid.) he said,
זֶה הַסּוֹמֵךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית;
One who joins Geulah to the Tefillah of Maariv."
So why did he change the wording,
writing there "Who is a ben Olam Haba,"
and here saying "He is assured," etc.?
So what was special about Rav Bruna,
that laughter did not leave his mouth
אָמַר לָהֶם כָּל שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד זְקֵנָיו כָּבוֹד,
He said to them, "Anyone before whose elders there is honor,"
of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, etc.;
in this world because of the wisdom of their old age";
and this is as they said (Kiddushin 32b),
"An elder is one who has acquired wisdom."
But it is not understood what he said,
I saw the upper ones below," etc.
אַךְ יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּקָאֵי עַל סִיּוּם דְּבָרָיו,
One could say that it refers to the end of his words,
"And how did you see us there?" etc.;
that there is a tradition from the Geonim
refers to Shmuel and Rav Yehudah;
וְעַל פִּי זֶה אֵינוֹ מוּבָן הַתְּשׁוּבָה
and according to this the answer is not understood,
"Anyone before whose elders there is honor,
since the incident would contradict it.
אַךְ נִרְאֶה דְּקָאֵי עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמַר
But it seems that it refers to what he said,
Fortunate is he who comes here
with his learning in his hand."
דְּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר אֵיזֶהוּ בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא
that what he said, "Who is a ben Olam Haba,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּחַיָּיו.
means one who is a ben Olam Haba in his lifetime.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א):
This is based on what they said (Berachos 17a),
"May you see your world in your lifetime";
for Olam Haba is the revelation
of the light hidden away for the tzaddikim for the time to come,
and that is the primordial light
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu hid away
and something of this light is revealed
time and again to the wise,
as written in the holy Zohar
even on each and every day,
for were it not for this light
the world could not endure," etc.
mem in the middle, tav at the end,
עַל שֵׁם אֲנִי רִאשׁוֹן וַאֲנִי אַחֲרוֹן.
corresponding to 'I am first and I am last.'"
And this corresponds to the Name Havayah:
א׳ הָיָה, מ׳ הֹוֶה, ת׳ יִהְיֶה.
alef, was; mem, is; tav, will be.
And it states in Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 4):
אוֹת ת׳ כּוּ׳ יוֹם שַׁבָּת בַּשָּׁנָה;
"The letter tav… the day of Shabbos in the year";
for Shabbos — the day that is entirely Shabbos —
דְּשֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים הֵם שֵׁשֶׁת אַלְפֵי שָׁנָה,
for the six days are six thousand years,
דְּיוֹמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶלֶף שָׁנָה;
since the day of HaKadosh Baruch Hu is a thousand years;
and the day that is entirely Shabbos is Olam Haba.
And in this world, Shabbos among the days
is a semblance of Olam Haba,
and this is the lower Shabbos;
and then the primordial light is revealed,
"He took a seventh part and set it for them in its place,
and the rest He hid away for the tzaddikim," etc.
And the beginning of the mishnayos is with mem, Me'eimasai,
and their end with mem, b'shalom;
וְהַתְחָלַת הַתַּלְמוּד, תְּנָא הֵיכִי קָאֵי, בְּת׳,
and the beginning of the Talmud, "Tanna heichi ka'i," is with tav,
And the mishnayos are also called halachos,
for they are the ways of the world,
to know the deed that he shall do;
and that is in the present,
as it is written, "For man goes
all the days of his life, toward his eternal home,
וְכָל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹלָם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
and each one has a world of his own
and this is through the halachos,
and likewise all the rulings of halachah,
And this is "who walk in the Torah of Hashem."
And this is what they said (Eruvin 54b):
"'And those who walk' — these are the masters of Mikra;
'on the way' — these are the masters of Mishnah;
'speak' — these are the masters of Talmud,
all of whose conversation is words of Torah."
For through the rulings of halachah
one can walk in the way of Hashem
and be secure in his path;
and that is in the aspect of "is," as was said.
"Speak" — these are the masters of Talmud,
who are steeped in words of Torah,
of those who toil in Torah
as written in the holy Zohar
for to them the light is revealed
which is of the hidden primordial light,
from every pleasure of this world
and are occupied only with Torah;
and as they said (Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3),
הָעָם הַהוֹלְכִים בַּחוֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל כּוּ׳,
"The people who walk in darkness have seen a great light," etc.,
And the Talmud begins with tav and ends with tav,
which is the aspect of "will be,"
that they merit their world in their lifetime,
which is the shining forth of the primordial light
hidden away for the time to come.
And this is "May you see your world in your lifetime":
שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
that they merit the revelation of the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
אוֹר הַגָּנוּז שֶׁהוּא עִיקַּר עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
the hidden light, which is the essence of Olam Haba,
And this is "Fortunate is he who comes here
with his learning in his hand":
that he has, in his lifetime, attainment of the light
that is a semblance of Olam Haba.
And this is what they asked Shlomo,
אֵיזֶהוּ בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא — בְּחַיָּיו, בְּהֹוֶה;
"Who is a ben Olam Haba" — in his lifetime, in the present;
אָמַר לָהֶם כָּל שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד זְקֵנָיו כָּבוֹד,
he said to them, "Anyone before whose elders there is honor,"
based on what they said in the Midrash
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה לח, ה; תַּנְחוּמָא תְּצַוֶּה ט):
and in none of them is 'honor' written
as it says, 'And Yaavetz was more honored than his brothers'
Because he toiled in Torah," etc.;
and he is Osniel ben Kenaz,
who restored through his pilpul the halachos
that were forgotten in the days of mourning for Moshe,
And on this the Gemara aptly brings,
אַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁבָּא לְכָאן וְתַלְמוּדוֹ בְּיָדוֹ,
"Fortunate is he who comes here with his learning in his hand" —
דְּזֶהוּ בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּחַיָּיו, וְכָאָמוּר:
for this is a ben Olam Haba in his lifetime, as was said.
זֶה הַסּוֹמֵךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית —
One who joins Geulah to the Tefillah of Maariv" —
the meaning is not the joining
which we were commanded to remember constantly, every day,
means to remember the shining forth of the light
that took place then at Yetzias Mitzrayim;
for with each of the plagues they came out of the kelipos
and entered the ten middos of kedushah.
And at the ninth plague it is written,
וּלְכָל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה אוֹר וְגוֹ׳
"But for all Bnei Yisrael there was light," etc.
and afterward, at the tenth plague,
And in the Geulah blessing one must mention
the plague of the firstborn and Krias Yam Suf
(as they said in the Yerushalmi, Berachos 1:6,
that the light of the first day should shine in the heart.
וְזֶהוּ מִצְוַת זְכִירַת יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בְּכָל יוֹם,
And this is the mitzvah of remembering Yetzias Mitzrayim every day,
in which one is like standing before a king —
and it is the Name Adnus that opens the mouth,
so that the Shechinah speaks from within his throat,
as written in Sefer Noam Elimelech
מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל (בְּרָכוֹת ז, א),
"From where do we know that HaKadosh Baruch Hu prays?" (Berachos 7a) —
that is, through the mouths of Bnei Yisrael.
this is an expression of being sent.
And with this the wording is precise,
"one who joins Geulah to the Tefillah of Maariv";
and why did he not mention that of Shacharis?
But at Shacharis, in joining Geulah to Tefillah,
meaning that it shines for him in the aspect of emes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רל, א):
"He is emes and She is emunah."
And at night, when it is not so clearly manifest
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אֱמוּנָה יְכוֹלִים גַּם כֵּן
for through emunah one can also
כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין בְּלִבְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָד וְכוּלֵּי
"Just as in your heart there is only One," etc.
(and this has been explained many times).
And at Shacharis, for one who joins Geulah to Tefillah,
it was not necessary to say
that he is a ben Olam Haba;
and about this he said of Rav Bruna
דְּלָא פָסַק חוּכָא מִפּוּמֵיהּ כּוּלָּא יוֹמָא,
that laughter did not leave his mouth the whole day,
(end of the first chapter of Taanis, 15a):
the righteous are for light," etc.,
וּכְתִיב אוֹר צַדִּיקִים יִשְׂמָח (מִשְׁלֵי יג, ט),
and it is written, "The light of the righteous rejoices" (Mishlei 13:9):
when light shines forth for him in the heart
and he attains uprightness of heart.
And day is in the aspect of emes, as was said.
He said it only to teach a novelty:
דְּאַף מִי שֶׁסּוֹמֵךְ גְּאֻלָּה לִתְפִלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית,
that even one who joins Geulah to the Tefillah of Maariv,
דְּהַגַּם שֶׁאֵין מֵאִיר לוֹ כָּל כָּךְ
although it does not shine for him so much
even in the aspect of emunah,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
he too is a ben Olam Haba.
And likewise on Shabbos, which is complete faith,
we say, "His light rests upon it";
"So too in our heart there is only One."
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין צח, א):
And this is the meaning of what they said (Sanhedrin 98a):
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְאֵלִיָּהוּ וְכוּלֵּי,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi found Eliyahu, etc.;
he said to him, "Will I come to the World to Come?"
אָמַר לֵיהּ: אִם יִרְצֶה אָדוֹן הַזֶּה.
He said to him, "If this Master wills it."
But what was he asking him?
הָא כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא!
All of Yisrael have a share in Olam Haba!
Rather, one may say that he asked
"destined for the life of Olam Haba" —
"What did he say to you?" He said to him,
"Peace be upon you, son of Levi."
He said to him, "He has assured you,
you and your father, of the World to Come."
But what is it about the "shalom" he said to him
that it should prove from it
But the matter is as we said:
"Will I come to the World to Come"
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר לוֹ אִם יִרְצֶה וְכוּלֵּי,
And to this he answered him, "If He wills," etc.,
for this depends on the will of Hashem Yisbarach
and not on the merit of deeds.
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג יב, ב):
And in the holy Zohar (Vayikra, Zohar III 12b):
"'Peace in His heights' — this is Yaakov,
דִּכְתִיב תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב (מִיכָה ז, כ),
as it is written, 'Grant truth to Yaakov' (Michah 7:20),
וּכְתִיב הָאֱמֶת וְהַשָּׁלוֹם אֱהָבוּ (זְכַרְיָה ח, יט),
and it is written, 'Love truth and peace' (Zechariah 8:19),
for truth and peace are bound to each other."
And regarding Yaakov, who merited light in the aspect of emes,
And likewise Pinchas, of whom it is written,
הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת בְּרִיתִי שָׁלוֹם (בְּמִדְבַּר כה, יב),
"Behold, I give him My covenant of peace" (Bamidbar 25:12),
according to the view that Pinchas is Eliyahu
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ אַבְטְחָךְ לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי:
And this is what he told him, "He has assured you of the World to Come":
that he would be able to merit Olam Haba while alive;
שֶׁנִּכְנַס רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי חַי לְגַן עֵדֶן
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi entered Gan Eden alive
he would attach himself to those afflicted with ra'asan
(as they said there in the Gemara).
And as for his saying "and your father":
because he called him by his father's name,
and it states in the Gemara (Megillah 15a),
כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ וְשֵׁם אָבִיו בִּנְבִיאוּת,
"Wherever one's name and his father's name are given in prophecy,
it is known that he is a prophet son of a prophet";
therefore he assured him regarding his father too,
that he is a ben Olam Haba in his lifetime.
Only, the one who actually merited this
דְּזֶה תָּלוּי אִם יִרְצֶה הָאָדוֹן, וְכָאָמוּר.
for this depends on whether the Master wills it, as was said.
וְכֵן כָּל הָאוֹמֵר תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד כּוּ׳
And likewise, "Whoever says Tehillah L'David, etc.,
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא —
is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba" —
this does not refer to what is recited alone,
the alef-beis, and "You open Your hand";
that is, the recognition shines for him
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach —
וְאָלֶף בֵּית מוֹרֶה עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
and the alef-beis signifies words of Torah.
וְעַל זֶה מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And for this he is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba,
meaning that he has not yet merited
but he is assured that he will merit
and to see his world in his lifetime.
And likewise here, at the conclusion of the Talmud,
and the conclusion of Maseches Niddah,
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה הַכֹּל עַל תִּיקּוּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
all of which signifies the rectification of the blemish of the bris,
מְסַיֵּים כָּל הַשּׁוֹנֶה הֲלָכוֹת בְּכָל יוֹם
it concludes, "Whoever studies halachos every day
מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא:
is assured that he is a ben Olam Haba":
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that through toil in Torah she'b'al peh
he will merit the blessing "May you see your world in your lifetime,"
to attain in his lifetime of the primordial light,
which is the reward of Olam Haba.
וְזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת מַאֲמָר זֶה לְסִיּוּם הַתַּלְמוּד,
And this is the connection of this statement to the conclusion of the Talmud,
which begins with tav and ends with tav,
which signifies the future, as was said;
and that through it he will merit
to see his world in his lifetime,
and to have his learning in his hand,
וּבְחַיָּיו יִהְיֶה בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא, כָּאָמוּר:
and in his lifetime he will be a ben Olam Haba, as was said.
